brand_names: Ravicti (note: Ravicti is glycerol phenylbutyrate, a related medication)
what_its_for: Sodium phenylbutyrate is used to help your body get rid of extra ammonia in your blood. It is used to treat a condition called urea cycle disorder (UCD), where your body cannot properly break down protein and ammonia builds up. Too much ammonia in your blood can be very harmful to your brain and body.
how_to_take: This medicine comes as tablets or a powder that you mix into food or drinks. Always take it with meals or feedings — do not take it on an empty stomach. If you are using the powder form, mix your prescribed dose into solid foods like applesauce or pudding, or into a drink like juice or formula. Never mix it into hot foods or drinks. Swallow tablets whole with water. Take all doses your doctor prescribed every day, even if you feel well.
dosing: Your dose is carefully calculated by your doctor based on your weight and medical condition. Most people take it in divided doses with each meal, usually 3 times a day. Never change your dose on your own. Your doctor will also ask you to follow a low-protein diet — this is a very important part of your treatment. Always follow the special diet plan your doctor or dietitian gives you.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if your next scheduled dose is not too soon. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are not sure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store tablets and unopened powder at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the powder tightly closed in its original container. Keep all forms of this medicine away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating large amounts of protein unless your doctor tells you otherwise — a low-protein diet is a key part of your treatment. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine. Avoid taking corticosteroids (like prednisone) or certain seizure medicines (like valproic acid) without talking to your doctor first, as they can raise your ammonia levels or interact with this medicine. Tell every doctor and pharmacist about all medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting anything new.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have any of these warning signs of high ammonia (called hyperammonemic crisis): extreme tiredness or unusual sleepiness, confusion, trouble thinking clearly, slurred speech, vomiting that won't stop, loss of coordination or balance, blurry vision, or loss of consciousness. Also call your doctor if you notice swelling in your hands, ankles, or feet (this medicine contains sodium/salt), unusual weight gain, or any new or worsening symptoms.
when_it_works: This medicine starts working to lower your ammonia levels within a few days of starting treatment, but it only works if you take it every day as prescribed and follow your low-protein diet. You may not feel any different right away, but your doctor will check your blood ammonia levels regularly to make sure the medicine is working. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, even if you feel fine.
special_populations: Children: This medicine is used in babies, children, and adults. Doses are carefully calculated by weight in children. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The risks and benefits need to be carefully discussed with your doctor. Older adults: Use with caution — older adults may be more sensitive to the sodium (salt) in this medicine, especially if they have heart disease, kidney disease, or high blood pressure. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have any kidney or liver problems, as this may affect how the medicine works in your body.
